AcpAuthenticatePayload.description:
`authenticate` request payload. `token` is absent only when the host has
no web auth token. Neither id is a credential.

protocolVersion.description: The protocol version the host speaks.

AcpRuntimePolicy.description:
Turn and keepalive budgets the host hands out at `authenticate`, in ms.
`0` means no limit for the two turn budgets.

AgentBackgroundCommands.description: The commands an agent left running, by owned session, as of `revision`.

AgentCapabilities.description: Agent capabilities as advertised at `initialize`. Unknown keys pass through.

AgentsWatchDelta.description: An `agents` delta: an agent-level fact with its event payload.

AgentsWatchEvent.description: The host fact an `agents` delta reports.

AuthCapabilities.description: Whether the agent can sign out.

BackgroundCommand.description: A command the agent left running after its tool call or turn ended.

startedAtMs.description: Wall clock when the tool call first appeared.

title.description: The command's description, else its tool call title.

BackgroundCommandList.description: One session's background commands as of `revision`.

CanvasLeaseLostReason.description: Why a renderer lost its canvas mount.

ChatActivityRecord.description: What every chat list shows for one agent chat.

busy.description: A prompt turn is open or the agent works outside one.

needsYou.description: A permission, question or elicitation waits for an answer.

projectId.description:
The project the session was created in; `null` when the host has no
persisted record of it.

unread.description: The newest turn end is past the shared last-read marker.

ChatActivityWatchDelta.description: A `chat_activity` delta: one session's record as it stands.

busy.description: A prompt turn is open or the agent works outside one.

needsYou.description: A permission, question or elicitation waits for an answer.

projectId.description:
The project the session was created in; `null` when the host has no
persisted record of it.

unread.description: The newest turn end is past the shared last-read marker.

ChatHistoryWatchDelta.description:
A `chat_history` delta: the sessions whose index entry changed, or an
empty list when the index changed in bulk.

ChatReadMark.description:
`mark_chat_read` request payload: a chat's shared last-read marker.
`logEpoch` is absent only from a peer that predates it.

ChatReadMarkReply.description:
`mark_chat_read` reply: the marker as it stands. Unlike the request it
accepts fields it does not name, so a client keeps reading the reply after
the host adds one.

ChatTurnEnd.description: The newest turn end the host saw for a chat.

DeleteSessionPayload.description:
`delete_session` request payload. The reply is `true` when the record was
deleted and `false` when it was already absent.

FsWatchChangeDelta.description: One debounced batch of changed paths under the project root.

FsWatchEndedDelta.description: The last `fs` delta: the project is no longer watchable.

FsWatchState.description: `fs` watch state: the canonical root being watched.

GitStatus.description: Change counts of a terminal's git working tree.

HistoryMode.description: Whether the host keeps session history.

PersistedSessionStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a persisted session.

continuedFrom.description: The session this one continues after an in-chat agent switch.

logEpoch.description: The session log's epoch. The hand-written type lacks it.

quickChatId.description: Host-minted folder id of a quick chat. The hand-written type lacks it.

startedBy.description: The chat whose agent started this one with `start_chat`.

titleSource.description: Who named the chat. The hand-written type lacks it.

turnActive.description: True while a prompt turn is open.

ProjectBusyDetails.description:
`err.details` of a `project_busy` refusal: the live sessions and terminals
bound to the project.

PromptCapabilities.description: Prompt content kinds the agent accepts.

RecordAgentSwitchPayload.description:
`record_agent_switch` request payload: the host appends one durable
`agent_switch` record built from it.

newSessionId.description: The session the conversation continues in.

ReliabilityTier.description: How the relay delivers an event type to a slow client.

SessionCapabilities.description: Which optional session methods the agent serves.

SessionCursorReply.description: `get_session_cursor` reply. An unknown session has no epoch and no head.

SessionSnapshotEvent.description: Atomic stale-recovery payload: the next cursor is `(logEpoch, watermark)`.

pendingMcpInstalls.description: MCP install approvals still waiting. The hand-written type lacks it.

SessionSubscribeReply.description:
`subscribe` reply. The `pending*` lists hold the original request payloads
still waiting for an answer, in queue order.

pendingMcpInstalls.description: MCP install approvals still waiting. The hand-written type lacks it.

SpawnedTerminal.description: `spawn` reply data: the terminal and the claim credential it issued.

claim.description: 64 hex characters; only spawn and rotate replies carry it.

StoreDeletePayload.description: `store_delete` request payload; shared keys follow the write preconditions.

StoreReadReply.description: `store_read` reply. Revision `0` means the key is absent.

StoreSharedWriteReply.description: `store_write` reply for a shared key: the stored, possibly merged value.

StoreWatchState.description: `store` watch state and delta: whether the key holds a value, and which.

StoreWritePayload.description:
`store_write` request payload. `expected: null` (key must be absent)
differs from no `expected`.

TerminalAttachResult.description:
`attach` reply data: the replay cursor and the terminal's last known
state. It never carries a claim.

TerminalSpawnOptions.description:
`spawn` request payload. With `program` set the PTY runs that executable
with `args` instead of a login shell. Unknown keys pass through.

TerminalStateSnapshot.description:
A terminal's last known state, sent on attach so a late client can seed
its store.

TerminalsWatchState.description: `terminals` watch state and delta: the project's terminals as they are now.

TitleSource.description: Who named a chat; a local alias wins over every other source.

UpdateProjectPayload.description:
`update_project` request payload. `cascade: true` stops the project's live
sessions and terminals instead of refusing `project_busy`.

UserPromptEvent.description: The payload of a `user_prompt` event: the user input the host recorded.

WatchResyncDelta.description: The delta the host sends when it could not queue the one before it.

WebTerminalDataFrame.description: One sequenced output chunk of an attached terminal.

WebTerminalErrorCode.description:
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE codes of `/terminal/ws` refusals. Handlers also
answer domain codes outside this set (`VALIDATION_ERROR`), so a reply's
`code` stays a string.

WebTerminalEventFrame.description: A terminal lifecycle or metadata change.

WebTerminalFrame.description: Any frame the host writes on `/terminal/ws`.

WebTerminalGapFrame.description: The output stream lagged and lost chunks after `lastSeq`.

WebTerminalReplayFrame.description: The chunks a client has not seen, sent on attach.

reset.description:
The cursor was from another epoch or ahead of the head: discard what
was rendered first.

WebTerminalReply.description: A reply frame: `data` on success, a message and a code on failure.

WebTerminalRequest.description: A request frame, client to host.

commandId.description:
Client-minted id of a ledgered request (`spawn`, `write`, `kill`,
`rotate_claim`, `revoke_claim`). A resend never runs twice.

payload.description:
The request payload; `spawn` sends a [`TerminalSpawnOptions`]. The
host accepts a request without one and reads it as `null`.

WsAgentSummary.description: One element of the `list_agents` reply. Older hosts omit the session lists.

ownsSession.description: Sessions whose workspace roots are registered on this agent's driver.

workingSessions.description: Owned sessions the agent works in outside a prompt turn.

WsCanvasAttached.description: The connection now runs the mount.

WsCanvasCallFrame.description:
One canvas control call for the connection that holds `projectId`'s canvas
at `mountSeq`, answered with a `canvas_reply` request.

params.description: JSON text, never parsed on the way.

timeoutMs.description: How long the host still waits for the reply, in ms. Absent on a notice.

WsCanvasError.description: The error of a failed canvas call.

WsCanvasLeaseLostFrame.description: The mount at `mountSeq` was saved and unmounted.

WsCanvasRefused.description:
The host has no such mount for this renderer. `heldElsewhere`: another
window holds the project's lease.

WsCanvasReplyPayload.description: `canvas_reply` request payload: the result's JSON text, or a typed error.

WsCanvasResult.description: A result, or one slice of it when `partial` is set.

WsError.description: The `err` object of a failed reply.

code.description:
A `WsErrorCode` string, or a SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE domain code from the
store and install handlers.

details.description: Set on `project_busy`: the live entities bound to the project.

WsErrorCode.description:
The stable snake_case `err.code` strings of `/ws`. Some handlers
(the store, installs) answer SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE codes outside this
set, so `WsError::code` stays a string.

WsEvent.description:
A session log event, host to client. `sid` is `null` and `seq` is `0` for
agent-level and relay-level events; `payload` is the camelCase ACP event.

WsEventBatchFrame.description: Several events queued together, written as one frame.

WsEventType.description:
The `type` of a `/ws` session log event. `gap` and `heartbeat` name the
top-level delivery frames. The host publishes every session-scoped ACP
event, so this list also holds the nine types after `heartbeat` that the
hand-written `WS_EVENT_TYPES` lacks.

WsGapFrame.description:
Lossy events of `sid` were dropped for this connection; the client installs
a fresh snapshot of the session.

WsHeartbeatFrame.description: The host is alive; written every 10 s.

visible_at.description: The session log seq the effect is visible at, on session commands.

WsReply.description:
A reply frame, host to client: success with an optional payload, or a
failure with a machine code.

WsRequest.description: A request frame, client to host. `id` is echoed in the reply.

command_id.description:
Client-minted id of a mutating request (1-128 characters of
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`). A resend with the same id never runs twice.

payload.description:
The request payload; its shape depends on `type`. The host accepts a
request without one and reads it as `null`.

WsServerFrame.description: Any frame the host writes on `/ws`.

WsTerminalSetEntry.description: One terminal of the `terminals` watch. It never carries a claim.

attached.description: A web connection holds a live attachment.

WsWatchFrame.description: A watch frame: exactly one of the full state and a delta.

WsWatchName.description:
A watch a connection can hold. `projects`, `chat_history`, `agents` and
`chat_activity` have the empty scope; `fs` and `terminals` are scoped
to a project id, `store` to a store key, `browser_screencast` to a tab id.

WsWatchRevision.description:
Which serve start produced a frame, and its position in the subscription's
stream: `n` is `1` for the full state and then rises by one per frame.

WsWatchStateFrame.description: The full state of a watch.
